correctness.rationale: Solving the two supporting-line equations in the (u_theta,v_theta) frame yields Z=h(theta)u_theta+[h(theta+alpha)-h(theta)cos(alpha)]/sin(alpha) v_theta. As alpha→0 the apparent pole cancels with limit h_prime(theta); only alpha=pi+delta creates norm ||Z||=w(theta)/|delta|+O_K(1), with derivative controlling exactly two tail intervals of half-width w/R+O(R^-2). Since iid arclength normal-angle density is rho/P, their flux is 2P^-2 int rho(theta)rho(theta+pi)w(theta), giving the sharp 1/R tail and q<1 moment criterion. The change of variables U=R/||Z|| has uniform leading derivative w/R, producing TV convergence of theta, fair side sign and uniform U; direction convergence is merely in probability, as stated. For constant width, rho+rho_antipodal=w and P=pi w, so algebra gives the square-defect identity and disk uniqueness. The smooth threefold-symmetric family rho=w/2[1+a tanh(k cos3theta)] has no first harmonic, strictly positive curvature and widths w; as a→1,k→∞ its coefficient tends to zero and continuity realizes every intermediate positive coefficient. Independent harmonic check h=1+epsilon cos3theta yields rho=1-8epsilon cos3theta and C=2/pi(1-32epsilon^2). Source quadrature is corroborative, not infinity-tail proof.

value.rationale: The intersection of two random supporting tangents is a natural integral-geometric statistic with heavy tails; the leading coefficient reveals antipodal curvature coupling, unlike width alone. The exact constant-width rigidity and full range answer a meaningful inverse-geometric stability question and show a sharp dependence on boundary sampling, beyond a routine circle calculation.

final_claim: For two independent arclength-uniform supporting tangents to any C^3 positively curved planar oval, P(||Z||>R)~C(K)/R with C(K)=2P^-2 int rho(theta)rho(theta+pi)w(theta)dtheta and a marked total-variation limit. At fixed constant width w>0 the exact defect is w/pi-C(K)=int(rho-rho_antipodal)^2/(2pi^2w); coefficients fill precisely (0,w/pi], uniquely maximized by a disk.
